11.ai_answer: The drought decreases supply (shifts supply curve left), while the health discovery increases demand (shifts demand curve right). Both effects push the equilibrium price higher. However, the effect on equilibrium quantity is ambiguous: decreased supply reduces quantity while increased demand increases it. The net effect on quantity depends on the relative magnitudes of the shifts. If the demand increase is larger, quantity rises; if the supply decrease is larger, quantity falls; if equal, quantity remains unchanged. Price will definitely increase.

12.ai_answer: When producers expect higher future prices, they have an incentive to withhold current supply and sell later when prices are higher. This decreases current supply (shifts the supply curve left). With demand unchanged, this results in a higher equilibrium price today and a lower equilibrium quantity today. Essentially, the expectation of future price increases becomes partially self-fulfilling in the present market as reduced current supply drives up current prices.
